plot: The day after the farm trip, Turbo's letter from the City Race Team invites him to a try-out at twelve, exactly when he promised to guard the school crossing; Grumpy's 'do both fast' plan nearly causes a near-miss, tiny Pip can't be seen holding the stop cone and finally admits she doesn't want him to go; Turbo keeps his promise and stays at the corner, and Coach Vera arrives there: the corner WAS the try-out, because the race needs a careful pace car on Saturdays only (clue planted: the letter said 'we saw you at the school corner'); lesson: keeping a promise is a win too; cliffhanger: Bolt forgets to tell anyone that the clocks go back tonight.

script.title: Is Turbo Leaving Wheelburg?!
script.description: Turbo's dream try-out is at the same time as his promise. Inspector Bolt #24

set.place: Wheelburg Main Street and the school crossing, Tuesday morning until noon, then evening at the town hall

beats.say: Woo-hoo! A letter from the City Race Team! For ME!
Leaving? Turbo, are you moving to the big city?
Try-out at twelve o'clock! If I win, I race there forever!
It was Tuesday morning in Wheelburg, the day after the farm trip.
And Turbo had already read his fancy letter eleven times.
Can I read it too? Just once?
It says... 'We saw you at the school corner on Monday.'
Of course they did! They saw my speed! Zoom, zoom!
But at the corner you go slowly. For the kids.
Details, Pip! Details! The city wants a champion!
Well done, Turbo. But twelve o'clock... isn't that your lunch shift?
My lunch shift? At the school crossing?
At twelve, the kids walk home for lunch. Turbo keeps them safe.
I promised Mrs. Maple I would never miss a shift.
But this is the City Race Team! It's my dream!
A big dream and a big promise. That's a heavy load, sweetie.
Easy. Do the shift fast. Then drive to the city fast.
Yes! Fast shift! Fast trip! Grumpy, you're a genius!
I know. Nobody ever says it. But I know.
So Turbo made a super-fast plan. And Pip didn't say a word.
He's leaving. And he looks so happy about it.
Pip. You can tell him how you feel, you know.
No. It's his dream. I don't want to spoil it.
At ten o'clock, Turbo practised his race start on Main Street.
Ready, steady... VROOOM! Did you see that, Wheelburg?
Turbo! Careful! I'm carrying the bakery's cakes!
Phew! Little kids can't jump away that fast, Turbo.
Sorry, Hal. I'm just... so excited.
One hour left! I leave at half past eleven!
And who will watch the crossing at twelve, dear?
Um. Someone? Grumpy? Bolt? Anyone with good brakes?
I tow cars at twelve. Cars don't tow themselves.
And I open the town hall at twelve. Procedure.
I'll do it! I'll hold the stop cone!
Pip rolled to the crossing. The cone was taller than her.
Stop, cars! Stop, please! Um... can anybody see me?
A delivery van drove right past. It never saw tiny Pip.
Oh no. I'm too small to keep the kids safe.
Pip! Are you okay?
I'm fine. I only wanted to help you go.
Because... I don't want you to go. But I want you happy.
You don't want me to go?
Who will race me to the bakery? Who will be silly with me?
Turbo looked at his letter. Then at the empty crossing.
Bolt... what do I do? Both things are important.
I can't choose for you, Turbo. But ask yourself one thing.
Which choice will you be proud of tomorrow?
Half past eleven. Time to leave for the city.
Turbo! Last chance! The city road is that way!
If I go, the kids cross the road alone.
A promise is a promise. I'm staying at my corner.
But... your dream, Turbo!
Dreams can wait. Kids crossing the road can't.
At twelve o'clock, the school bell rang. Ding, ding!
Turbo stood at the crossing with his big stop cone.
Stop, please! Kids crossing! Thank you! Have a yummy lunch!
Then a shiny teal car rolled up and parked. She watched.
Excuse me. Are you Turbo? The car from my letter?
Yes. But I can't come to the try-out. I'm sorry.
Oh, you didn't miss it. This IS the try-out.
I'm Coach Vera. Our race needs a pace car.
A car who leads the racers and stops them if someone's in danger.
On Monday I saw you stop for the kids. Every single time.
That's what the letter said! 'We saw you at the school corner!'
Today I wanted to see one thing. Would you keep your promise?
And you did. The job is yours. Saturdays only.
Saturdays only? So I don't have to leave Wheelburg?
You're staying! Turbo's staying!
Hooray! Honk, honk! That's our Turbo!
Good. Who else would I complain about?
Keeping a promise is a win too, Turbo.
Pip! Race you to the bakery after lunch? Winner gets a cookie!
That evening, Bolt found a note on the town hall door.
'Tonight the clocks go back one hour.' I must tell everyone!
But a gust of wind took the note away. Whoosh!
And Bolt was so happy for Turbo, he forgot to tell anyone.
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
